matches.note: Winner gets a World Title shot at Live and Loud 3. Entrants came in on a countdown, tag teams entering as one; Kenny Mercury drew number one. Three slots went unfilled or changed hands: the Local NVA Company's (laid out backstage), Bruce Gordy's (arrested; Tommy Waters and then E Razor came in instead) and Lew Spectre's (he sent Doctor Franken in his place). matches.stipulation: UWF World Heavyweight Championship Match — No Disqualification, No Countout, Anything Goes
matches.note: Main event, refereed by I.M. Referee. Pete the PG Tips Chimp, the champion, came to the ring at the controls of a giant robot dragon, accompanied by Maurice; Seymour Almasy walked down hand in hand with Aerith Heartilly and, using his Divine Blade Imperial II in a match for the first time, cut off the dragon’s tail to break a pin and hacked through its foot until it toppled out of the ring. The Plague laid Almasy out with a barbed wire chair, and Ben Jericho first broke up a moonsault pin and then hit Almasy with the title belt and dropped him with two powerbombs and a reverse piledriver on it, but Almasy kicked out each time. He pinned Pete with Aerith’s Elbow, after the Via Purifico spinebuster, to win the UWF World Heavyweight Championship. Aerith embraced him in the ring; Kenny Mercury and Ben Jericho attacked him until Crab Mask, Jr. and Max Queue, swinging Big Ted’s Arm, made the save, and Almasy and Max Queue formed the tag team RPQ~!, with Crab Mask, Jr. joining them as a stable.

For the THC (Hardcore) Championship. The Plague, already hurt and wheeled to ringside, came out under threat of being fired; the champion Joshua Dunn attacked him with a chair, a 2x4 and a fan’s pen, stabbed into his temple, but froze before the Ten Dunn Salute, and the Plague hit the Black Death and won the title by pinfall.

For the UWF Television Championship, staged at the foot of “Mt. Gagazet”: the belt hung at the summit and the first man to take it won. Seymour Almasy and Tsunami Oni fought from the ring up the mountain; near the top a Ronso drove its spear into Oni’s head, and Almasy took the belt (20:34). The Ronso unmasked as Aerith Heartilly, whom Oni had taken from him.

matches.note: Main event. Seymour Almasy, the champion, v. Kevin Starr, the Regal Rumble winner, inside a steel cage around the ringside area with a sword on a pole at each corner of the ring; no pinfalls, won only by knocking the other man out. Almasy, who had asked Aerith Heartilly to stay backstage, took the PTC Global title belt to the face at the bell and Starr's Super Starr Slam; he hit the Omnislash, went into Trance, sliced through Starr's Buster Sword with his Divine Blade Imperial II and knocked Starr out cold with the flat of the blade to retain the World Heavyweight Championship. Aerith ran to him at the end.

matches.note: A best-of-three series for the number-one contendership to the Intercontinental title. The Plague won the hardcore fall, pinning Adien Pryde after hitting him with a chunk of the broken announce table; Pryde made The Plague submit to the Sibko Streacher in the submission fall and won the deciding fall with the Falcon Driver.

matches.stipulation: North American/Intercontinental/THC Title Match (Triple Title Triple Ladder Match. Pluck a Title Out of the Sky and Exit Match as Champion of Said Title)
matches.note: Misfit, the Intercontinental Champion, did not appear and Moraless, the North American Champion, was absent. Nick Persia dropkicked over the ladder Kenny Mercury stood on, throwing him into the fifth row. Clyde, whom Richard Hayes afterwards named Misfit’s replacement, choke-slammed Killer Dude and left with the THC title. Nick Persia swung a ladder into Seymour Almasy, the THC Champion, as he hung from the rings, and Almasy fell holding both the Intercontinental and North American belts; Hayes restarted the match as a two-fall contest for those two titles. Persia pinned Killer Dude with the Dutch Destroyer for the Intercontinental title, and Almasy, playing possum, pinned Killer Dude with a small package to keep the North American title.

Main event, refereed by Jerry ‘Pops’ Kohler; Mike Montgomery came out with El Chupacabra. Montgomery hit the Hangman's Joke and pinned Jamie Shock with the Fall From Grace from the top rope, and the booth called the night a sweep for the Player's Club over the Prime Alliance.

matches.note: El Baiano (the registry’s El Bianno; the card spells him both ways), Lyle Wile’s Brazilian capoeira proxy, debuted against Hot Mask, who worked his legs with a Texas Cloverleaf and pinned him with a small package; Lyle Wile then dragged El Baiano backstage.

A five-team elimination brawl for the World Tag Team Titles with no disqualifications and no count-outs. Rich Rollins’s partner was Angelo Deville, making his UWF in-ring debut. Rollins pinned Eric Cameron with an Anarchist Elbow off The Communist’s shoulders, eliminating the champions, The Phenomenons; Mike Montgomery eliminated The Communist and Digital Mortality with the Fall From Grace onto a chair; Deville pinned Montgomery after he and Rollins chaired everyone. Left with Clyde against Rollins and Deville, Seymour Almasy survived a Doomsday Device and Deville’s Soprano (broken when Tsunami Oni misted both), flattened Deville with a plancha to the floor, and Clyde pinned Rollins after a chokeslam backbreaker across Almasy’s knee: the Dark Ages won the titles.

Wes Diable’s debut, refereed by the Rabbi of Pain: Diable reached the ropes out of the Infection and reversed the Black Death, then rolled The Plague up with a schoolboy while he argued with the referee.
Killer Dude retained the North American Championship against the Intercontinental Champion, Nick Persia: after a chair shot and a lariat he pinned Persia holding a handful of tights.

Before the bell Hot Mask brought out a boy in a church robe who tasered Wes Diable; Nick Persia ran in to clear the ring and the bell was rung with both men inside. Diable won by pinfall with the Shooting Star Press he calls The Urgency, beating the Intercontinental Champion in a match that was not for the title and advancing in the Contest of Champions tournament.
A three-way. Mike Montgomery hit the Fall from Grace on Digital Mortality and pinned him.

Seymour Almasy's answer to Killer Dude, who had taken the North American Championship from him a few weeks earlier; the title was not on the line. Almasy caught Killer Dude's charging spear and powerbombed him, dominated, and won by pinfall after the Gallows, taking his place in the Contest of Champions.

Tsunami Oni (c) defended against Ezra Kazee. The Chaos Society's Raid interfered for Kazee, but Oni blinded him with the mist and Raid hit Kazee with the Bug Bomb by mistake; Oni then made Kazee submit to the Onipocalypse.

Main event, refereed by Graham ‘Cracker’ Poll and introduced by the ring announcer, Tommy Waters. Seymour Almasy offered a handshake, Hot Mask tried a joke with it, and Almasy pulled him in and drove a knee into his stomach; he then worked over Hot Mask’s shoulder and survived Hot Mask’s figure four with two shoulder-up kickouts. When Eve and Lilith of S.H.E.M.A.L.E. came back to the ring and Hot Mask let go to cover himself, Almasy took him down with a schoolboy for the pin and the Television Championship, ending Hot Mask’s 79-day reign; it was Almasy’s third Television title. Afterwards Kenny Mercury fisherman-suplexed Hot Mask onto the Intercontinental title belt on the floor, Richard Hayes announced Lew Spectre against Tsunami Oni at The Clash, and Spectre unmasked Hot Mask; Almasy ran back into the ring to help the man he had just beaten and hit Mercury with the title belt, and was beaten down with chair shots by Spectre and belt shots by Mercury.

Television Title Match, refereed by IM Referee and introduced by the ring announcer, Tommy Waters. The challenger Deuce overpowered Seymour Almasy, the champion, early with a clothesline, a slam and a leg drop, but hit the ring post when Almasy sidestepped a corner charge, and Almasy then worked on the shoulder with a single-arm DDT, knee drops and a Fujiwara armbar. When Deuce fought free and lifted him for a powerbomb, Almasy blasted him in the face with the Firaga, unseen by the referee, and made him submit to the Fallen Wings. Almasy stomped Deuce’s injured shoulder after the bell and retained the Television Championship.

Ezra Kazee, billed with Fizbane the Fabulous, was found laid out backstage before the match and took no part, so Fizbane wrestled alone against both teams. Clyde and Duke Williams kept turning on each other. Nick Persia came through the crowd and hit the referee, Clyde, Duke Williams and Fizbane with a steel chair, and Malcolm Kennedy then pinned Clyde: Tsunami Oni and Malcolm Kennedy won.

Richard Hayes booked a retirement handicap match after Chris Storm announced his retirement. The crowd was led to expect Seymour Almasy and Kenny Mercury: Almasy’s entrance music played, then Mercury’s, and neither came out. The two masked men who ran in were The Violator and Scourge, and Hayes and Storm laughed together that it was a set-up. Storm hit both with a steel chair in front of the referee and the match ended in a disqualification, the first win of the careers of The Violator and Scourge.

Wonder Boys (Jamie Shock and Kenny Mercury) defended the World Tag Team Championship against Anarchy (Adien Pryde and Reo Dai), refereed by the Rabbi of Pain and introduced by the ring announcer, Tommy Waters. Anarchy jumped the champions before the bell and nearly won with a double-team powerbomb and a Dragon Strike into a bridged German suplex, but Shock mule-kicked Reo Dai, superkicked Adien Pryde, and Kenny Mercury caught Pryde in the Spell-Binder; Pryde was left motionless and the referee called for the bell. The champions retained.
“Big” Dick N. Uranus retained the Television Championship: Adien Pryde attacked him from behind and hit the Falcon Driver, but Uranus kicked out and pinned Pryde with a Death Valley Driver.

Seymour Almasy and Duke Williams fought to a double count-out: Almasy’s hurricanrana from Williams’s shoulders sent both to the concrete, Graham Poll counted both out as they kept brawling, and Mucho Macho Security had to separate them.

Main event, a steel cage match. Lew Spectre came to the ring with Aerith Almasy, Seymour Almasy’s former wife. Seymour Almasy came down and threw a steel chair into the cage; Aerith held him off by kissing him, and when he reached the top of the cage and leapt with the chair, both men moved and Almasy crashed to the mat. Spectre and Montgomery briefly turned on Almasy together before Spectre made Montgomery tap to the Figure Four Sleeper. Afterwards Richard Hayes booked Almasy against Montgomery in a No Disqualification Match, Montgomery chaired Almasy, Aerith chaired Montgomery, and Tsunami Oni, Nick Persia, Malcolm Kennedy, Misfit and Shiatsu overran Spectre and the Wonderboys.

A triple threat for the UWF Television Championship: Silvio Rochelli against the champion, “Big” Dick N. Uranus, and Jagger Vince. Rochelli pinned Uranus with the Fall from Grace to become the new Television Champion.

Clyde, Almasy’s former tag team partner, withstood a sharpshooter, a tornado DDT, a slingshot moonsault and a top-rope moonsault; the two men downed each other with a Firaga and a fireball at the same moment and rose just before the ten count. Clyde powerbombed Almasy out of a dragonrana, choke-slammed him, and pinned him with The Gallows. Afterwards Mike Montgomery, Almasy’s opponent at The Clash a week later, choked him unconscious with The Blackout while he tapped.

Under hardcore rules; Misfit, the THC Champion, did not have the title on the line. Duke Williams opened by breaking a whiskey bottle over his head; Misfit answered with a senton onto a chair on the floor and survived the Whisky Shot onto the broken glass. Kenny Mercury ran in and beat both men with a steel chair; the text records no decision.

A four-on-four elimination battle royal; Mike Montgomery, injured, was at home. Draco Paladine powerbombed Ezra Kazee, and Raid and Adien Pryde hit Kazee with steel chairs behind the referee's back, so that he was stretchered out. The Squadron went through to the finals.

Kevin Starr pinned Richard Ray Vaughn first; Digital Mortality made Seymour Almasy tap to the Digitizer; Corporal Punishment made Bondage the Sex Fiend tap to the Lethal Injection; Starr pinned Moraless after a double facebuster with Joshua Dunn; Kenny Mercury pinned Malcolm Kennedy after Ruff Ryder powerbombed Kennedy from the top turnbuckle through the announce table; Angel, back for the first time since 2000, attacked Digital Mortality and left; Starr rolled up Mercury; the Corporal, bleeding and swinging his cattle prod, eliminated Nick Persia, Ezra Kazee and Kevin Starr with the Lethal Injection; and Dunn pinned the Corporal with the Ten Dunn Salute and then rolled up Digital Mortality, holding the tights, to win Stable Wars for the Player's Club. matches.note: Malcolm Kennedy and Nick Persia won the World Tag Team titles from the Wonderboys (Jamie Shock and Kenny Mercury), refereed by the Rabbi of Pain. Mercury sprayed Persia with “Precision” and Shock felled him with a crowbar, but Persia was not the legal man; Shock shoved the referee, the Rabbi shoved back, Shock stumbled over Persia, and Kennedy rolled him up with a schoolboy for the pin.

Main event. Lew Spectre, back from a long hiatus, beat the ring announcer Tommy Waters before the bell, dragged I.M. Referee into the path of Tsunami Oni’s chair and broke the fingers of the second referee, Jerry Kohler; Graham Poll’s count on Oni’s Onipacalypse was broken up by Kenny Mercury, and the Wonderboys joined the attack. Corky Spectre, Lew’s self-proclaimed son, stood on the chair Lew was reaching for, and Oni rolled Lew into a backslide that Corky counted: Tsunami Oni retained the World Heavyweight Championship.

matches.note: “Sick” Rick Daniels, billed as the Intercontinental Championship’s number one contender, beat Skull, making his first UWF television appearance, by pinfall with the Sickness (4:24).

Six-man tag team match scheduled for one fall, refereed by Earl Hebner: Digital Mortality and the Dragoons (Eiji Kanatsu, “Tiamat”, and Bahamut) against Killer Dude and the Gangstars (Razor, who has no iwf/giwf/uwf record, and Blade 2). Killer Dude begged for the tag and got it; Digital Mortality laid into him until the Masked Canadian slid into the ring behind the referee and hit Killer Dude with a Diamond Cutter, and Digital Mortality pinned him. From the crowd afterwards the Masked Canadian told Killer Dude he would find out at Zero Tolerance what the Masked Canadian was about.

UWF Television Title defence, refereed by James Beard: Deke Aurora (c) against “2Xtreme Kid” John Bennett, led to the ring by Sapphire. Aurora attacked Bennett before the bell and won with the High-Angle Jack-Knife Powerbomb (0:04:42), retaining the title.

Tag team match scheduled for one fall, refereed by Danny Davis: Corporal Punishment and Luke “Jaxx” Shinoda (teaming up for the first time; Richard Hayes walked them to the ring, both wearing their UWF belts) against Jamie Shock (led to the ring by Sarah) and the Plague. With Shock and Cpl. Punishment in the ring and a near-fall at one, two, thr… kickout, Hayes took the Intercontinental belt from the announcers' table and smashed the referee across the back of the head with it; Jaxx clotheslined Shock and Punishment booted the Plague. The bout never reached a decision: Hayes then had Punishment hold Shock in the Lethal Injection (over four minutes) while he beat him with the belt, and left him bleeding.

Opening match, refereed by Earl Hebner: Snake Phoenix (Los Angeles, 310 lbs) against Rob Roblou (Newark, 175 lbs), whom two well-dressed men had pushed into a barrier on the way in. Snake Phoenix won by pinfall in 2:06.
Refereed by Danny Davis: Killer Dude (Green Bay) against “Sick” Rick Daniels (Des Moines), Killer Dude having promised a first win in a long time. Killer Dude won by pinfall in 5:20.
One fall, refereed by Tim White: “-Da Bomb-” Danny Jaye (Memphis) against Joshua Dunn (Falkirk, Scotland). Jaye won by pinfall in 6:27, extending the winning streak he had announced.

UWF Television Title match, refereed by Tim White: Deke Aurora (c) against Lyle “In Style” Wile, the former GIWF World, Intercontinental and Television Champion and Aurora's one-time Youngbloods team-mate, meeting him in the UWF for the first time. The referee threatened Wile with disqualification and three times removed a chair from the ring; neither man could put the other away and the bell rang for the time limit: a time-limit draw, Aurora keeping the title. Earlier in the night Aurora had come through the crowd, locked Danny Jaye in the Romero Stretch and named him as his Zero Tolerance opponent.

Intercontinental Title match, refereed by James Beard: Corporal Punishment against Digital Mortality, a re-match of the Christmas Capers title match. Digital Mortality was giving as good as he got when he threw the Corporal across the ring and a hooded figure pulled the top rope down, sending the Corporal to the floor: the Masked Canadian, who hit him with a Diamond Cutter and jabbed him repeatedly with a cattle prod, rolled him back into the ring and left through the crowd, promising to humiliate him at Zero Tolerance. Officials and EMTs ran to the ring. No fall, count or decision was given.

matches.note: Over-the-top-rope battle royal, advertised as an eight-man main event, to decide who enters at number 30 in the Regal Rumble at Zero Tolerance. Deke Aurora came out and withdrew, declaring himself number 1 in the Rumble; Richard Hayes announced he would not compete (“a Presidential Favour” for Aurora; Hayes stayed at ringside), leaving six men in the ring. Jamie Shock eliminated Gurgles, the Plague threw out Digital Mortality, went over the top himself when his clothesline on Luke Shinoda missed, then climbed the apron and pulled Shinoda out. Corporal Punishment and Shock were left; Hayes climbed the apron to pull Shock's arm, Shock decked him, and Corporal Punishment threw Shock over the top rope to win the number 30 spot.

Refereed by Earl Hebner: Jamie Shock (led to the ring by Sarah, who distracted his opponent twice) against Blade, whom the booth called a thorn in Shock's side and the Youngbloods' weakest link. Shock beat Blade by pinfall in 7:00.

Tag team match scheduled for one fall, refereed by Earl Hebner: Team MIV (Dex, the Television Champion, and Flip) against Slasher and Digital Mortality. Flip and Dex dived under the ring; Slasher and Digital Mortality were then bombarded with coloured paint from all sides of the arena and ran up the ramp, and Flip and Dex crawled out. No fall was counted and no decision given. Flip then asked Dex to put his TV title aside and team for the tag titles, and Dex agreed.

Tag team match scheduled for one fall, refereed by Tim White: the debuting Local NVA Company (Thai Trang, spelled “Tai Trang” in the play-by-play, and Duc Chu Song) against the Forces of Darkness, the former GIWF World Tag Team Champions, here Jared Crafter and Tombstone. Trang held the Forces off with a jumping DDT and a Liger Bomb on Tombstone; Duc Chu Song rolled Tombstone up with a backslide after a cobra clutch was countered, and pinned him. The Local NVA Company won.

A triangle match against Justin Time and “Renax” Rob Jenks. Killer Dude rolled Rob Jenks up in a bridging reverse cradle with both men’s shoulders on the mat, and the referee counted three on both: “Both combatants have been pinned!” No winner was announced (5:17).
Seymour Almasy defended the UWF Television Championship ten days after winning it. Purple Haze made him submit to the Spell-Binder and won the title (13:30).
A two-on-one handicap match. Lance Rose made Fat Bastard submit to the Rose Perfume (16:18).

2-on-1 handicap match scheduled for one fall, refereed by the Rabbi of Pain: Samantha Vale (Minneapolis, 154 lbs) against Miami Missile and Wildlife (Wildlife has no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Shiatsu blew her a kiss from the ramp afterwards.

Tag team match scheduled for one fall, refereed by Jerry Kohler: the Wimp & Chimp Connection (Maurice and Pete the PG Tips Chimp) against the Alaskan Warriors (Avalanch and Iceberg; Iceberg has no iwf/giwf/uwf record). Pete the Chimp finished it with the Chimpy Chompy Crunch on Avalanch, who submitted; the referee called for the bell (0:18:32). The Wimp & Chimp Connection won.

Match for the vacant UWF Television Championship, refereed by Graham Poll: Moraless against Steel. Moraless locked Steel in a submission and Steel nodded when asked whether the fight should be stopped; Poll stopped it (0:17:37). Moraless won and became the new Television Champion.

Main event, a tag team match scheduled for one fall, refereed by I.M. Referee: the Legends (Luke Warren and Lance Rose) against the Drowning Pool (Slasher and “Unforgiven” Ben Jericho), with World Champion Danny Jaye walking out to stand at ringside as the bell rang. Bill Alfonso distracted each Legend in turn. Late on, the Legends stopped to stare at the big screen, which showed Jack Union pounding on Sam Gordan's door; Lance Rose slid out of the ring and Jaye caught him on the floor and tossed him back in. Slasher pinned Lance Rose (0:27:15); Luke Warren had left his partner and is next seen at Gordan's door. The Drowning Pool won.
